title: vnodes node record (schema v2.1)
description: One machine, as every source describes it: an admin by hand (vnodes add), an enrolment kit run on the node, a capability probe, and later discovery. All of them emit THIS record. Other projects may vendor this file byte-for-byte and reference it by this $id, which pins the version. The inventory (nodes.schema.json) additionally requires status, admin_group and provenance, which vnodes writes. Never holds keys, tokens or passwords. 2.1 is additive over 2.0: every 2.0 node is a valid 2.1 node.

id.description: Stable identifier. Never changes once added; never reused after retirement.

name.description: Short hostname. v1 readers match it against `hostname -s`.

host.description: Resolvable name when different from `name` (v1 field).

ssh.description: SSH target or alias as typed (v1 field). `local` = the controller itself; `none` = not reachable by SSH.

user.description: Login user on the node (informational, v1 field).

owner.description: The principal who owns the node (v2.1): the person who answers for it, e.g. the operator who ran the kit on it. Derived from an OS login, never typed. Distinct from admin_group (who administers) and user (login used to reach it).

os.description: Operating system family. 'windows-git-bash' (v2.0) is accepted but deprecated: validators warn and `vnodes export` emits os=windows + shell=git-bash. With windows-git-bash, shell may only be git-bash.

shell.description: Login shell agents and installers should use on the node (v2.1). Optional; consumers default to powershell on windows and bash elsewhere.

role.description: Coarse profile for tools that install per-node defaults (v1 field).

roles.description: What the node does in the fleet. Consumers resolve a role to its holders (see docs/CONSUMERS.md).

primary_for.description: Roles where this node wins when several nodes hold them. Must be a subset of roles.

enabled.description: Operational pause (sync/push tools skip enabled=false). Distinct from status=retired.

mcp_profiles.description: Named tool profiles a configuration tool should wire on this node.

addresses.description: Names preferred; IPs optional. No discovery fills these in this phase.

admin_group.description: OS group whose members administer this node.

capabilities.description: Declared by hand in this phase. A later capability probe may only PROPOSE changes as plans.

basis.description: declared = typed by an admin; probed = accepted from a capability probe plan.

services.description: Services the node hosts, e.g. a model server, a gateway, a database.

card.description: Reserved slot for a signed node card (mDNS / DNS-SD / signed-manifest discovery, not implemented; see docs/DISCOVERY.md): the card's node_id and host-key fingerprint, and the admin who approved the join. Written only when an admin applies a discovery plan. Empty until then.

provenance.description: Written by vnodes on apply. Never hand-edited.

change.description: plan id (or 'genesis') of the last change to this node

actor.description: An identity derived from the OS login (pwd/grp via NSS) at the time of the action. Never typed.

principal.description: Who, as a string: user:<login>@<node-id>. <login> is the OS account name exactly as the OS reports it for the running process (POSIX: getpwuid(getuid()) through NSS, so local, SSSD, authd and Kanidm accounts all work; Windows: the account name of the current WindowsIdentity without the DOMAIN\ prefix). Never typed, never read from $USER/$USERNAME. <node-id> is the inventory id of the node that account lives on. Same identity rule as the vnodes admin check. Examples: user:alice@ctl-1, user:Alex Example@alex-pc. Other kinds (group:, service:) are reserved for later versions.

enrolment.description: How the node entered the inventory (v2.1). Written once with the add; never changed afterwards. Independent of provenance, which vnodes keeps writing on every change.

source.description: manual = an admin ran vnodes add; kit = from an enrolment kit request; probe = capability probe proposal; mdns = discovery (not implemented).

at.description: When the record was made (kit: request created_at; manual: proposal time).

by.description: Who started the enrolment: the operator who ran the kit on the node, or the admin who proposed it.

request_sha256.description: kit: sha256 of the enrolment request file the record came from.
